translationRepairs: Chang Qing directed naval commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to enter from Luerhmen, vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to move with Haizhen garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou from Tamsui, and department commander Ma Yuanxun to hold Lugang, dividing his forces along several axes.

Chang Qing directed naval commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to enter from Luerhmen, vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to move with Haitan garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou from Tamsui, and department commander Ma Yuanxun to hold Lugang, dividing his forces along several axes.
The source titles Hao Zhuangyou 海壇鎮總兵; 海壇 is Haitan, so Haizhen drops 壇 and is a naming error. The proposed replacement is otherwise unchanged and accurate.

Chang Qing ordered Naval Commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to advance from Luerhmen, Vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to accompany Haizhen garrison commander-in-chief Hao Zhuangyou advancing from Tamsui, and Department Commander Ma Yuanxun to encamp at Lugang, deploying forces along separate routes;

Chang Qing ordered Naval Commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to advance from Luerhmen, Vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to accompany Haitan garrison commander-in-chief Hao Zhuangyou advancing from Tamsui, and Department Commander Ma Yuanxun to encamp at Lugang, deploying forces along separate routes;
The same 海壇鎮 is misread as Haizhen in the literal field; Haitan is the correct place name and the rest of the sentence is sound.
In the seventh month Chang Qing ordered Panlong to relieve Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the throne appointed him commander of the Haizhen garrison.
In the seventh month Chang Qing ordered Panlong to relieve Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the throne appointed him commander of the Haitan garrison.
The throne’s appointment is 海壇鎮總兵; Haizhen is a mistranscription of 海壇, and Haitan restores the garrison name without other changes.
In the seventh month, Chang Qing ordered Panlong to reinforce Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the emperor ordered him appointed commander of the Haizhen garrison.
In the seventh month, Chang Qing ordered Panlong to reinforce Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the emperor ordered him appointed commander of the Haitan garrison.
Literal English likewise renders 海壇鎮 as Haizhen; the source is the Haitan garrison command, and the proposed wording is accurate.
The court proposed sending him back to his former post as commander of the Haizhen garrison.
The court proposed sending him back to his former post as commander of the Haitan garrison.
海壇本任 is Panlong’s original Haitan post; Haizhen is the same 壇 misreading, and the replacement matches the Chinese.
That winter he reinforced Grand Coordinator Hengrui at Yanshui Harbor, burned rebel strongholds, and was named Fenyong Batulu.
That winter he reinforced military consultant Hengrui at Yanshui Harbor, burned rebel strongholds, and was named Fenyong Batulu.
參贊 here is a campaign staff commission, not 巡撫. Grand Coordinator is a different office; military consultant correctly identifies Hengrui’s role.
That winter he reinforced Grand Coordinator Hengrui at Yanshui Harbor, destroyed rebel stockades, and was granted the title Fenyong Batulu.
That winter he reinforced military consultant Hengrui at Yanshui Harbor, destroyed rebel stockades, and was granted the title Fenyong Batulu.
The literal field repeats Grand Coordinator for 參贊; the source names Hengrui as 參贊, a military consultant, not a provincial xunfu.
In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Coordinator Shu Chang against Ripang and earned credit.
In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Minister Consultant Shu Chang against Ripang and earned credit.
The office is 參贊大臣, a campaign grand minister consultant, not Grand Coordinator. The proposed title matches the Chinese.
In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Coordinator Shu Chang in attacking Ripang, with merit.
In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Minister Consultant Shu Chang in attacking Ripang, with merit.
Literal English makes the same 參贊大臣/Grand Coordinator error; Grand Minister Consultant is the accurate office for Shu Chang.
At Tongpanzhan Chaoxiong led the van in a sortie; Intendant Yongfu and Subprefect Yang Tingli followed with soldiers and militia, cut down another hundred-odd rebels, and put the enemy to flight.

When rebels attacked Tongpanzhan, Chaoxiong led the van in a sortie; Intendant Yongfu and Subprefect Yang Tingli followed with soldiers and militia, cut down another hundred-odd rebels, and put the enemy to flight.
The Chinese opens 賊攻桶盤棧; the original omits the rebel attack and treats Tongpanzhan only as a location. The replacement restores that clause without adding other matter.
Fuk'anggan memorialized his merit, and he was made garrison commander of Haizhen.
Fuk'anggan memorialized his merit, and he was made garrison commander of Haitan.
授海壇鎮總兵 appoints him to the Haitan garrison; Haizhen is again a misreading of 壇.
Fuk'anggan reported his merit; he was appointed garrison commander of Haizhen.
Fuk'anggan reported his merit; he was appointed garrison commander of Haitan.
The literal field has the same Haizhen error for 海壇鎮; Haitan is the correct garrison name.
He followed Grand Secretary Agui in suppressing the Muslim uprising at Lanzhou and was granted the honorific title Fashishang Batulu.
He followed Grand Secretary Agui in suppressing the Muslim uprising at Lanzhou and was granted the honorific title Fashishang'a Batulu.
法什尚阿 must keep 阿 (Fashishang'a). This chapter already renders 巴圖魯 as Batulu (Fenyong, Qiangsheng, Chongjie); changing only this title to Baturu is an unnecessary romanization shift.
He followed Grand Secretary Agui in pacifying the Lanzhou Muslim rebellion and was given the title Fashishang Batulu.
He followed Grand Secretary Agui in pacifying the Lanzhou Muslim rebellion and was given the title Fashishang'a Batulu.
The missing 阿 is a real error, but Baturu would break this chapter’s established Batulu spelling of 巴圖魯; restore Fashishang'a Batulu.
In the third year Governor-General Lebao again impeached him for ineffective pursuit of rebels; he was dismissed but kept his soldiers with the army.
In the third year Governor-General Lebao again impeached him for ineffective pursuit of rebels; he was dismissed but retained with the army as a common soldier.
以兵丁留軍 means he himself was retained in the ranks as a soldier after dismissal, not that he kept command of his troops. The idiomatic field already has this, and the proposed literal is accurate.
E Hui and Shu Liang marched under Fuk'anggan, and Panlong and Chaogui each won his share of battlefield credit.
E Hui and Shu Liang marched under Fuk'anggan, and Panlong and Chaoxiong each won his share of battlefield credit.
The paired names are 攀龍、朝雄. 朝雄 is Ding Chaoxiong, not 朝桂 (Liang Chaogui); the replacement corrects the misidentification.
E Hui and Shu Liang followed Fuk'anggan on campaign, and Panlong and Chaogui each had battle achievements;
E Hui and Shu Liang followed Fuk'anggan on campaign, and Panlong and Chaoxiong each had battle achievements;
Literal English likewise reads 朝雄 as Chaogui; the source names Chaoxiong, and the proposed wording is correct.
